policy.queueAuthorityNote: CORRECTED TWICE. fd86823 seeded 'V5_WORKSTREAM_REGISTRY_AND_MASTER_REMEDIATION_WAVES'; no such registry has ever been committed in any branch or history. Milestone 3 replaced it with three documents, which was still INCOMPLETE: it omitted the authority for owner decisions and for closure evidence. All five documents above declare themselves 'Wave 0 deliverable', state their own scope, and cross-reference each other as companions -- MASTER_REMEDIATION_REGISTRY names all four others. They are a closed, self-declaring set, so naming five rather than three changes no governed decision. Whether a V5_WORKSTREAM_REGISTRY was ever INTENDED remains an open owner question: evidence of absence does not establish intent.
policy.requireAttestedIdentityNote: Left false deliberately. No runner exists to mint identity tokens, so enabling it would block all verification. Turn it on when a runner holds SKILLS_AGENT_ATTESTATION_KEY out of worker reach.
policy.inventoryScopeNote: SCOPE CORRECTED, Milestone 6. The earlier ten tasks modelled only the autonomous-team infrastructure and the governance blockers -- ZERO product remediation work. The registry's board carries ~177 READY_TO_REMEDIATE rows (canonical total 319 = 37+48+24+177+4+29), none of which were represented. The five tasks added below are the WAVE-LEVEL product work at the current frontier, each traced to the wave plan or the registry. This is still NOT a per-row enumeration of the 177: the registry states that the P1-P3 register carries no per-row status field and its movement is not mechanically countable, so a per-row queue cannot be derived without inventing statuses.
